Answer: C
Reason: The clinical context of a rapid decrease in end-tidal CO2 during vertebroplasty strongly suggests pulmonary cement embolism, and the provided CT images (Figures 4a and 4b) clearly show hyperdense material within the pulmonary arteries consistent with polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) cement. While the chest X-ray findings can be subtle, the presence of dense intravascular material on cross-sectional imaging confirms the diagnosis of cement embolism.
